senses.gloss:
mokṣa
(‘liberation [from transmigratory existence]’)
------------------------------------------
The topic of बन्ध (bondage) and मोक्ष (liberation) has been widely discussed in all the systems of Hindu philosophy.
Man is essentially the आत्मन्, the pure spirit, of the nature of चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स्; but has somehow forgotten it and has identified himself with the body-मिन्द् complex. As a result, he is constantly undergoing transmigration, the cycle of birth-death-rebirth and so on. Whatever suffering a man undergoes, is due to this identification with the body and the मिन्द्, and consequent transmigration brought about by कर्म.
This cycle of transmigration, called ‘saṁsāra’, can be ended only by the realisation of the आत्मन्. This again is achieved by the destruction of अज्ञान or अविद्या (ignorance) through ज्ञान (know-ledge). Once this is done, मोक्ष is attained.
Of course, there are other schools which advocate niṣkāma कर्म (action not motivated by selfish desires) or भक्ति (devotion to God resulting in his grace) as the means to मोक्ष.
Mokṣa is posited as the final puruṣārtha, the ultimate goal of life.
The synonyms for मोक्ष are: मुक्ति, कैवल्य and निर्वाण.
See also BANDHA.
Some works like the Sūtasaṁhitā (Muktikhaṇḍa 3.28) describe four kinds of मुक्ति or मोक्ष as follows: सालोक्य (living in the same world as God); sārūpya (having a form similar to that of God); सामीप्य (living near God); सायुज्य (getting identified or united with God). These ideas seem to have existed in the Vedic literature itself (vide Taittirīya Saṁhitā 5.7.5.7; Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 2.24; Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.3.22; Chāndogya Upaniṣad 2.20.2).

Mokṣadharmaparva
------------------------------------------
The Mahābhārata has 18 parvas or books or sections, of which the Śāntiparva is the biggest. It contains the teachings of भीष्म from his bed of arrows to युधिष्ठिर in reply to the various questions put by the latter.
The Mokṣadharmaparva is a subsection of the Śāntiparva and comprises the Chapters 174 to 365. It deals with a variety of topics connected with spiritual life including मोक्ष or लिबेरतिओन्.
See also MAHĀBHĀRATA.
